name: AI Pigeon Meme
tagline: Turns a short text prompt into an 8-second AI pigeon clip you can download and post.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a prompt box, a themed system prompt, and a billing wrapper around someone else's text-to-video model. The UI is genuinely a one-sitting build: a form, a job queue, a gallery, a download button. The catch is the part that makes the clips, which is a hosted video model you rent per second, so your personal version still has a hard third-party dependency and a per-clip cost that does not go away. Where the product earns its keep is the invisible work: a pigeon-shaped system prompt that stops the model from producing uncanny bird soup, plus sane defaults for aspect ratio, duration, and watermark-free output. Build it if you want control over the prompt template, not if you expect it to be free.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that takes a short prompt, wraps it in a fixed pigeon-themed template, calls a hosted text-to-video model, and saves the resulting 8-second MP4 to a local gallery.
requirements: An API key for a hosted text-to-video model (fal.ai, Replicate, or Google Veo via API)
A credit card, because video generation is billed per clip and is not cheap
Node 20+ and local disk for the MP4 files
Patience for prompt iteration: the first twenty pigeons will look wrong
whatYouLose: A tuned pigeon prompt template that someone already spent a hundred failed generations refining
Hosted queueing and retries when the model provider times out or rejects a prompt
Mobile-friendly polish and instant social-ready export presets
Any content filtering, so your DIY version will happily render whatever you type
Zero marginal effort: you now own the API bill, the key rotation, and the storage
moatNotes: The only durable asset is prompt craft and defaults, and prompt craft leaks the moment someone screenshots an output.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the product is cheaper than curiosity. Nobody who wants one pigeon meme for a group chat is going to open a model provider account, add a payment method, and iterate on prompt wording for an hour. Paying a few dollars for a working button that reliably produces the specific absurd thing you wanted is a fair trade, and the themed constraint is a feature: a narrow generator with good defaults beats a general one you have to steer yourself.
notes: The app is a thin shell over a rented model, which is also exactly why your shell works fine.
prompt:
Build a local-only web app called "pigeon-studio" that generates short AI pigeon meme videos from text prompts.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind, single app, no separate backend.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for job records. No ORM.
- Video generation through fal.ai's HTTP API using the @fal-ai/client package and a text-to-video model (default to a fast 5-8 second model, make the model id a single constant at the top of lib/video.ts so it can be swapped).
- MP4 files written to ./storage/clips and served from a route handler. Do not commit storage.

What it does:
- One page: a textarea for a short idea (max 200 chars), an aspect ratio toggle (9:16, 1:1, 16:9), and a Generate button.
- Server action wraps the user text in a fixed pigeon template stored in lib/prompt.ts, for example: "cinematic 8 second clip, a single city pigeon, {idea}, handheld camera, natural daylight, photoreal, no text overlay". Keep the template in one editable file and export it.
- Create a job row (id, idea, final prompt, aspect, status, file path, created_at), call the model, poll until done, download the MP4 to ./storage/clips/{id}.mp4, mark complete. On failure store the provider error text and show it verbatim.
- Gallery below the form: newest first, inline video players, download link, delete button that removes row and file.
- Show estimated cost per clip as a hardcoded constant next to the button so the bill is not a surprise.

Explicitly out of scope: accounts, auth, payments, sharing links, watermarks, telemetry, Docker, cloud storage, content moderation.

Secrets: FAL_KEY in .env.local only, read server-side, never exposed to the client. Include .env.example.

Deliver a README with: pnpm install, how to get a FAL_KEY, pnpm dev, where files land, and a one-paragraph warning that each generation costs real money and that prompt quality is the whole game.
